neighbours.label: The token ' restraint' and its family (' restrain', ' restrained', ' restraining', 're|straints'). Near-synonyms (patience, self-control) and the look-alike ' constraint' are quiet.
fire: The governor urged both sides to exercise restraint over the weekend.
Two nurses had to restrain the patient until he calmed down.
Her speech was praised for its restraint and quiet humour.
The dog was restrained by a short leather lead.
Central banks have shown little restraint in printing money.
It took three guards to restrain the angry fan.
Every child seat must have a working restraint across the chest.
With visible restraint, the coach declined to criticise the referee.
quiet: The governor urged both sides to exercise caution over the weekend.

The dog was held back by a short leather lead.
Central banks face a tight constraint in printing money.
It took three guards to remove the angry fan.
Every child seat must have a working buckle across the chest.
With visible self-control, the coach declined to criticise the referee.
